title: Introduce composite weighted regression metric and CI hook for prompt-level evaluations
author: Marta Kim
description: Motivation: current CI gating looks at single metrics (e.g. exact-match or average score) which misses regressions concentrated on high-impact queries or on small but important slices. This PR adds a composite, weighted regression metric (CWScore) that aggregates multiple eval metrics at the prompt/query level with configurable per-query weights and historic-baseline smoothing, and wires a CI hook to fail builds when the composite regression exceeds policy thresholds. Design summary: (1) new metrics/composite.py implements CWScore with pluggable metric adapters and support for query-level importance weights supplied via the prompt-set metadata; (2) persistence/compat shim to ingest historic baselines from previous eval artifacts (S3/GCS keys) and apply exponential smoothing to reduce noise from single-run variance; (3) a CI hook ci/hooks/composite_regression_hook.py that runs as part of eval CI, computes delta vs baseline, applies per-repo thresholds (.eval-ci.yml opt-in), and supports a tolerant mode that posts warnings instead of failing when the regression is small but persistent; (4) unit and integration tests and docs. Checklist: - [x] implement composite metric and adapters - [x] add CI hook and config parsing - [x] add baseline smoothing + backfill helper - [x] add unit tests and a small integration test against synthetic eval artifacts - [x] update docs and quickstart - [x] include Linear ticket reference. Usage notes: opt-in by adding "composite_metric: true" and optional "weight_key" to prompt-set metadata; default weight_key is "importance". Default gating policy is 1.5% relative regression on CWScore for blocking failures; tolerant mode sets action: warn. Safety: when prompt metadata lacks weights, CWScore falls back to uniform weights; when historic baseline is unavailable CI will create the baseline on first successful run (not fail). Related tasks: ENG-5223 (primary), ENG-5330 (follow-up dashboarding). This description is intentionally compact and single-line for PR body export.
